package_info.why_malicious: WarmCookie is a two-stage Windows backdoor distributed via phishing and fake browser update campaigns. It provides attackers with remote access, data exfiltration, command execution, and the ability to deploy further payloads, all without user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Collect CPU identification and memory size, then send to C&C server via HTTP POST.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code queries system hardware information (CPU ID, memory size), then sends this data to a remote C&C server via HTTP POST, enabling system fingerprinting.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting and exfiltrating hardware information to an external server is a common reconnaissance step in malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently send hardware fingerprints to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise asset management tools may inventory hardware, but with user/admin consent and to trusted endpoints.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Take a screenshot of the desktop and send the image to the C&C server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On C&C command, the code captures a screenshot of the victim's desktop and exfiltrates the image to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote screenshotting is a classic surveillance and data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not take screenshots and send them to remote servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may take screenshots, but only with explicit user permission.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Enumerate installed programs via Uninstall registry key and send results to C&C.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On C&C command, the code queries the Windows registry for installed programs and sends the list to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Enumerating installed software is a reconnaissance step for further exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software inventory tools do not send this data to untrusted servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT management tools may inventory software, but only to trusted infrastructure.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Execute arbitrary shell commands via cmd.exe /c and send back results via HTTP POST.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On C&C command, the code spawns cmd.exe to execute arbitrary shell commands, captures the output, and sends the results to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command execution is a hallmark of backdoor malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not execute arbitrary shell commands from remote instructions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may execute commands, but only with strong authentication and user awareness.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Read arbitrary files and send contents to C&C; write files to disk on command.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On C&C command, the code reads specified files and exfiltrates their contents, or writes attacker-supplied files to disk.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Arbitrary file read/write and exfiltration is a direct data theft and persistence technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not allow remote parties to read or write arbitrary files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may transfer files, but only with explicit user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Write DLL to %TEMP% and execute via rundll32.exe, sending output to C&C.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On C&C command, the code writes a DLL payload to the %TEMP% directory, executes it using rundll32.exe, and sends the output to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping and executing DLLs is a common malware technique for code injection and privilege escalation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not download and execute DLLs from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may use DLLs, but only from trusted sources and with user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware copies its own executable to the %TEMP% directory, likely for persistence or evasion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-replication to temporary directories is a common evasion and persistence tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers may use %TEMP%, but not for self-replication post-install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Installers may extract files to %TEMP% during setup.

attack_chain.action: User is lured via phishing email or fake Chrome update site to download and execute WarmCookie (Install_x64.exe).
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial execution of malware on victim system

attack_chain.action: Malware fingerprints the system (CPU, memory) and sends data to C&C.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains knowledge of victim environment

attack_chain.action: Malware takes a screenshot and exfiltrates it to C&C.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains visual context of victim's desktop

attack_chain.action: Malware enumerates installed programs and sends list to C&C.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker assesses installed software for further exploitation

attack_chain.action: Malware receives and executes arbitrary shell commands from C&C, sending results back.
Malware reads or writes arbitrary files on disk, exfiltrating data or deploying new payloads.
Malware writes DLLs to %TEMP% and executes them via rundll32.exe, sending output to C&C.
Malware copies itself to %TEMP% for persistence or evasion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential for re-execution or evasion of detection

behavioral_signatures: Executable downloaded from browser update-themed phishing sites
Immediate outbound HTTP POST to suspicious domains after execution
Enumeration of installed programs via registry access
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for executables downloaded from known phishing or fake update domains. Detect processes that immediately make outbound HTTP POST requests to suspicious infrastructure. Alert on processes that capture screenshots, enumerate installed software via registry, or execute arbitrary commands via cmd.exe /c. Watch for DLLs dropped and executed from %TEMP% using rundll32.exe. Correlate file creation in %TEMP% with subsequent suspicious process activity.
